construct: The diaphragm forms from multiple embryologic components, including the septum transversum, pleuroperitoneal folds, dorsal mesentery of the esophagus, and body-wall musculature. Failure of posterolateral pleuroperitoneal-fold fusion creates a Bochdalek defect, permitting abdominal viscera to enter the thorax and compress the developing lung, causing pulmonary hypoplasia and pulmonary hypertension.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A newborn with scaphoid abdomen, bowel sounds and bowel loops in the left chest, and severe respiratory distress has a left posterolateral congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: The septum transversum contributes to the central tendon, but the classic Bochdalek posterolateral defect is due to failure of pleuroperitoneal-fold closure/fusion.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The posterolateral location and neonatal pulmonary-hypoplasia phenotype make pleuroperitoneal-fold failure uniquely correct.
